A minion matching the new villain’s title is discarded; if a matching-title minion is revealed while that villain is already in play, discard the minion and reveal an additional encounter card.

Protect the Morlock allies. They do not count against ally limits and cannot leave play through card abilities, but can still be defeated by damage. Watch the main scheme’s knock counters: reaching their threshold has a different advancement effect from reaching the threat threshold.

setup.title: Morlock Siege — Campaign Setup
bullets: Record every player’s identity. Those identities remain fixed for the entire campaign.
As a group, choose one of the six campaign player side schemes, put it into play, and record the choice for scenario 1. Shuffle its paired encounter card into the encounter deck.

victory.title: Morlock Siege — Victory
bullets: Record the titles of the defeated Marauders under Routed. They will be unavailable as villains in On the Run.
Record how many Morlock allies remain in play. Each one saved grants a deck search in the next scenario.
Mark any campaign environment still in play as earned.

intro.title: On the Run — Hope’s Captor
text: The Morlocks have survived the assault, but the retreating Marauders have captured Hope. The attack may have been a diversion to seize her.
At an abandoned construction site, the Marauders are handing Hope over to Mister Sinister’s Nasty Boys. Her captor tries to escape while the other mercenaries cover the retreat.

rules.title: On the Run — Scenario Rules
bullets: One of the remaining Marauders is chosen at random as this scenario’s villain. The Hope’s Captor attachment begins Confident-side up.
Hope’s Captor means the villain must be defeated twice to win. Its first defeat flips the attachment and restores the villain’s printed hit points rather than ending the game.
The Mutant Slayers encounter set is required. Military Grade and Nasty Boys may be replaced when customizing the scenario.

setup.title: On the Run — Campaign Setup
bullets: Before the main scheme chooses a villain, remove each Marauder villain recorded as defeated. Minions with those same titles remain in the encounter deck.
For every saved Morlock, choose a player to search their deck for a card, add it to hand, and shuffle. A player may be chosen more than once.
If a campaign environment was earned, put it into play and give each enemy a tough status card.
Choose a previously unchosen campaign player side scheme and record it for scenario 2. Put it into play, then shuffle every chosen scheme’s paired encounter card into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: On the Run — Expert Campaign Setup
text: Begin with the hit points recorded after the previous victory. Each player may add one acceleration token to heal their identity to full hit points. A defeated player uses this option to rejoin.

victory.title: On the Run — Victory
text: Hope is free. Mark each campaign environment still in play as earned; those rewards carry into Juggernaut.

intro.title: Juggernaut — The Orphanage
text: Hope’s captor reveals where she was to be delivered: the State Home for Foundlings in Omaha. Hope refuses to wait at the X-Mansion while the heroes investigate, so she accompanies them.
The orphanage appears deserted until its doors burst outward. Juggernaut stands in the entrance, blocking the way inside.

rules.title: Juggernaut — Scenario Rules
bullets: Momentum counters increase Juggernaut’s ATK. The action on Juggernaut’s Helmet offers a way to remove momentum, and the counters carry over when a villain stage is defeated.
The Hope Summers set is required. Black Tom Cassidy is also required when playing this scenario as part of the campaign.
Hope must remain in play. Keep her safe while finding a way past Juggernaut.

setup.title: Juggernaut — Campaign Setup
bullets: Put all earned campaign environments into play in any order, then place one momentum counter on Juggernaut for each campaign environment in play.
Shuffle Black Tom Cassidy with one Creeping Willow per starting player. Deal one of these cards facedown to each player and shuffle the remaining card into the encounter deck.
Choose a previously unchosen campaign player side scheme, record it for scenario 3, and put it into play. Shuffle all chosen schemes’ paired encounter cards into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: Juggernaut — Expert Campaign Setup
text: Begin with the hit points recorded after the previous victory. Each player may take one facedown encounter card to heal their identity to full hit points. A defeated player uses this option to rejoin.

victory.title: Juggernaut — Victory
bullets: Record the amount of damage on Hope Summers. That damage affects the next scenario.
Mark every campaign environment still in play as earned.

intro.title: Mister Sinister — Beneath the Orphanage
text: Past Juggernaut, a hidden elevator descends beneath the abandoned orphanage. Its doors reveal a sprawling laboratory filled with medical machinery and unconscious captives in glowing vats.
Mister Sinister waits among his experiments. Stop him before he can use the stolen mutant powers for his own ends.

rules.title: Mister Sinister — Scenario Rules
bullets: The Flight, Super Strength, Telepathy, and Hope Summers sets are required. The three Superpower attachments are set aside during this scenario’s setup, so their Setup keywords do not place them into play at the start.
The three Sinister Experiments stage-2 main schemes each correspond to a Superpower encounter set. One stage is removed at random, and the other two are put in a random order.
In expert mode, resolve Sinister Intent’s When Revealed first. It advances to the first random stage 2 and reveals both faces. Resolve Mister Sinister II’s When Revealed afterward.

setup.title: Mister Sinister — Campaign Setup
bullets: Put all earned campaign environments into play in any order. Put Teleported Away into play and add one threat per starting player for each campaign environment in play.
Choose whether Hope takes damage equal to her recorded damage from Juggernaut, or Teleported Away gains that much threat.
Choose a previously unchosen campaign player side scheme, record it for scenario 4, and put it into play. Shuffle all chosen schemes’ paired encounter cards into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: Mister Sinister — Expert Campaign Setup
text: Begin with the hit points recorded after the previous victory. Each player may add one acceleration token to heal their identity to full hit points. A defeated player uses this option to rejoin.

victory.title: Mister Sinister — Victory
bullets: Record the damage on Hope Summers for the final scenario.
Mark every campaign environment still in play as earned.

intro.title: Stryfe — Through the Portal
text: Before Mister Sinister can be taken into custody, he escapes through a time portal. Hope follows him, determined to stop his plans. The heroes follow to protect her.
Beyond the portal, Sinister lies unconscious at Stryfe’s feet. Stryfe, a clone of Cable, overwhelms Hope with telepathic power. Her attempt to copy his powers threatens to end in an explosion.

rules.title: Stryfe — Scenario Rules
bullets: For effects referring to the most common card type in your hand, count the cards of each type. If types are tied for the largest count, either tied type has that same count.

Stryfe’s constant ATK bonus updates when the contents of the attacked player’s hand change, until attack damage is determined. Playing a damage-prevention event after that point does not recalculate damage already determined.
The Hope Summers set is required. Protect her throughout the battle; her departure loses the game.

setup.title: Stryfe — Campaign Setup
bullets: Put all earned campaign environments into play in any order. Add one threat per starting player to Stryfe’s Grasp for each campaign environment in play.
Choose whether Hope takes damage equal to her recorded damage from Mister Sinister, or Stryfe’s Grasp gains that much threat.
In player order, each player discards encounter cards until finding a minion or Psionic attachment, then reveals that card. Afterward shuffle the encounter discard pile into the encounter deck.
Choose a previously unchosen campaign player side scheme, record it for scenario 5, and put it into play. Shuffle all chosen schemes’ paired encounter cards into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: Stryfe — Expert Campaign Setup
text: Begin with the hit points recorded after the previous victory. Each player may take one facedown encounter card to heal their identity to full hit points. A defeated player uses this option to rejoin.
If the heroes lose this game, Stryfe escapes into the past and the expert campaign is lost.

victory.title: Stryfe — Victory
text: Stryfe is defeated and the heroes win the NeXt Evolution campaign. Read the conclusion.

campaignMode.title: Age of Apocalypse: Campaign Mode
text: Apocalypse rules an alternate North America, and the heroes must overthrow him and undo the events that created this future. Play Unus, Four Horsemen, Apocalypse, Dark Beast, and En Sabah Nur in that order.

Keep the same identity throughout the campaign. Between games, you may change aspects and customize the rest of your deck under the usual deck-building rules. Follow normal scenario setup, then its campaign instructions. Resolve victory instructions before continuing.
Losing a scenario permits another attempt without a campaign penalty. The final victory has an extra requirement: winning the battle alone is not enough to save Professor X.
bullets: Campaign-specific cards enter decks only when the campaign instructs you to add them. Mission rewards marked as exempt do not count toward the minimum deck size.

The campaign log remembers attempted missions, their outcomes, defeated Overseers, and each hero’s rewards. A mission already attempted is unavailable later; only defeating an Overseer removes that Overseer from the pool.

expertCampaign.title: Age of Apocalypse: Expert Campaign
text: After a victory, record each surviving identity’s remaining hit points, capped at its base hit points. This becomes that identity’s starting health in the next scenario.

During later setup, a player may place 3 threat on the current mission to restore their identity to full health. A player eliminated from a game their teammates won does not receive its victory rewards; they can rejoin next time by taking this threat-for-healing option.
In every expert campaign setup, the ally searched for must share at least one trait with the player’s hero. It still counts toward the opening hand size.

expertSetup.title: Expert Setup: Health and Starting Ally
bullets: Restore the hit points recorded after the preceding victory. Each player may place 3 threat on the mission to heal to full health; an eliminated player uses this option to return.
The starting ally you search for must share a trait with your hero, even though setup begins in alter-ego form. This ally replaces a card in your opening hand rather than adding an extra card.

expertVictory.title: Expert Victory: Persistent Damage
bullets: Record surviving identities’ remaining hit points, never more than their base hit points. A player eliminated during this scenario does not take its victory rewards and must use the mission-threat recovery option to return next game.

missionRules.title: Side Missions and the Mission Area
text: Side missions represent crises elsewhere in Apocalypse’s empire while your heroes confront the villain. Your allies, rather than your identities, attempt them.

For the first four scenarios, select a random unused mission and an available Overseer. The finale instead uses Protect the Professor. The first player controls Mission Team; its action either discounts the next ally played to the mission this phase by 2, or makes a mission attempt.
bullets: The mission area is separate from player areas. Its cards are in play but uncontrolled, and abilities can affect them only when they explicitly refer to the mission area. Ordinary thwarting cannot remove mission threat.

When playing an ally while a mission is unfinished, choose to play it under your control or into the mission area. Mission allies do not count toward the ally limit. Their printed text is blank except for traits, but upgrades can be attached to them.
Mission enemies do not activate like engaged minions. An Overseer cannot be damaged while another mission minion remains, and the mission cannot be defeated while any mission minion remains.
Mission Response abilities are forced responses that resolve after cards are discarded for an attempt, before those cards are assigned to allies.

missionAttempts.title: Making a Mission Attempt
bullets: Exhaust Mission Team to make the attempt. Discard one card from the acting player’s deck for each ally at the mission, then resolve the Overseer’s Mission Response.

Assign each discarded card to a different mission ally. An ally participates if an icon on its assigned card matches an icon on that ally; a wild icon on either can match any resource icon. Multiple icons do not let one card be assigned more than once.

Add the participating allies’ modified ATK into one damage pool and distribute it among mission enemies, choosing the amount for each enemy. Then remove mission threat equal to those allies’ combined modified THW.

A mission can be defeated only with no mission enemies remaining and no threat on it. On success, shuffle the player cards at the mission into their owners’ decks, then flip the mission and Mission Team and resolve the printed result.

After an unsuccessful attempt, add an attempt counter and deal 1 damage to each remaining mission ally. The fourth unsuccessful attempt removes Mission Team and finishes the mission as a failure. Resolve its result and clear the mission area as instructed.
After a successful mission, the completed side of Mission Team stays with the first player and can exhaust to let a player draw a card.

keywords.title: Featured Rules
bullets: “Find” means search each area where the card could be, without looking at facedown encounter cards dealt to players. You need not search areas unnecessarily when its location is known.
Teamwork makes an entering minion activate against its engaged player if another minion sharing the named trait is in play. Villainous gives a minion a boost card for its activation.

Hinder adds threat when its card enters play. Patrol prevents its engaged player from using controlled cards to thwart the main scheme. Stalwart prevents stun and confuse; steady requires two matching status cards before the character is stunned or confused.
Defeated cards with victory go to the victory display. Each amplify icon adds a boost icon to a boost card when that card is turned faceup during an enemy activation.

If Standard III is selected, Pursued by the Past begins in play and its counters determine when nemesis sets enter. Standard III may replace the original Standard set; it is not an extra encounter set used alongside it.

conclusion.title: Campaign Victory: Professor X Is Saved
text: Protect the Professor succeeded, and En Sabah Nur is defeated. The heroes obtained what they needed to save Professor X and won the campaign.

failedConclusion.title: Campaign Defeat: Professor X Was Not Saved
text: Although the heroes won the battle, Protect the Professor was not completed. Professor X was not saved, so the campaign is lost.

intro.title: Scenario 1: Unus
text: X-Force’s rescue mission for Hope Summers has stranded them in a changed timeline. Apocalypse rules this future, and his prelate Unus and the Infinites attack the displaced heroes.

rules.title: Unus: Scenario Rules
text: The Infinites modular set is required. Gene Pool begins in play and is permanent; threat on it strengthens both Unus and the Infinite Soldier. Watch its changing thresholds rather than treating its threat as harmless.
The guide offers optional starting threat on Gene Pool to tune the challenge. The standard campaign uses the scenario’s configured setup; no extra difficulty adjustment is required.

setup.title: Unus: Campaign Setup
bullets: Record the heroes chosen for the campaign. Each player keeps that identity for all five scenarios.

After normal scenario setup, shuffle the Age of Apocalypse encounter set into the encounter deck. Select an unused mission and an available Overseer, following the mission’s campaign-log setup instructions.
Put the mission and Overseer in the mission area. The first player takes control of Mission Team on its Mission side.
Each player searches their deck for an ally to add to their opening hand. This ally counts toward the opening hand size. Expert campaign players must choose an ally sharing a trait with their hero.

victory.title: Unus: Campaign Victory
bullets: Mark this mission as attempted so it cannot be selected in a later scenario. Apply its success or failure instructions in the campaign log; the selected result is shown below.
If the Overseer was defeated on its Overseer face, remove that Overseer from the campaign pool. Defeating its Prelate face does not count.

intro.title: Scenario 2: Four Horsemen
text: Magik and Bishop rescue X-Force and bring them to the X-Men’s hidden headquarters. Magneto explains that Professor X’s assassination allowed Apocalypse to rise, and that the resistance has been slowly losing the war.
Before Magneto can explain his plan, Apocalypse’s Four Horsemen breach the headquarters. The new allies must survive the assault together.

rules.title: Four Horsemen: Scenario Rules
text: War, Famine, Pestilence, and Death enter in random order. Only the active villain normally activates during the villain phase; the active marker passes to the next villain on the right after an activation, wrapping from the end of the row to its beginning.

Encounter effects and constant abilities referring to “the villain” mean the active villain. When a player triggers a player-card ability referring to “the villain,” that player chooses which villain it targets. Players may attack any Horseman, and specific card effects can activate a Horseman that is not currently active.
Standard play uses each Horseman’s A side; expert play uses B sides. All four must be defeated to win.

setup.title: Four Horsemen: Campaign Setup
bullets: After normal scenario setup, shuffle the Age of Apocalypse encounter set into the encounter deck. Select an unused mission and an available Overseer, following the mission’s campaign-log setup instructions.
Put the mission and Overseer in the mission area. The first player takes control of Mission Team on its Mission side.
Each player searches their deck for an ally to add to their opening hand. This ally counts toward the opening hand size. Expert campaign players must choose an ally sharing a trait with their hero.

victory.title: Four Horsemen: Campaign Victory
bullets: Mark this mission as attempted so it cannot be selected in a later scenario. Apply its success or failure instructions in the campaign log; the selected result is shown below.
If the Overseer was defeated on its Overseer face, remove that Overseer from the campaign pool. Defeating its Prelate face does not count.

intro.title: Scenario 3: Apocalypse
text: With the Four Horsemen defeated, Magneto leads X-Men and X-Force against Apocalypse himself. The heroes must cross the old city of New York and break through the tyrant’s citadel, opposed by his army and strongest prelates.

rules.title: Apocalypse: Scenario Rules
text: Apocalypse regenerates instead of being defeated unless No Longer Worthy is attached to him. This attachment is the reverse of The Tyrant’s Throne. Advance the scenario’s objective and reveal it before delivering the winning blow.
Without that attachment, a would-be defeat discards his attachments, heals him, and removes the amount of main-scheme threat specified by the scheme, ignoring crisis icons. It does not win the game.
Prelate minions are the reverse faces of the Overseers. Defeating a Prelate during the main scenario does not remove its Overseer face from the campaign’s mission pool.

setup.title: Apocalypse: Campaign Setup
bullets: After normal scenario setup, shuffle the Age of Apocalypse encounter set into the encounter deck. Select an unused mission and an available Overseer, following the mission’s campaign-log setup instructions.
Put the mission and Overseer in the mission area. The first player takes control of Mission Team on its Mission side.
Each player searches their deck for an ally to add to their opening hand. This ally counts toward the opening hand size. Expert campaign players must choose an ally sharing a trait with their hero.

victory.title: Apocalypse: Campaign Victory
bullets: Mark this mission as attempted so it cannot be selected in a later scenario. Apply its success or failure instructions in the campaign log; the selected result is shown below.
If the Overseer was defeated on its Overseer face, remove that Overseer from the campaign pool. Defeating its Prelate face does not count.

intro.title: Scenario 4: Dark Beast
text: Apocalypse’s defeat throws his empire into turmoil. While prelates compete for power and the oppressed rise up, the heroes search beneath the citadel for a time portal that could undo this future.

The scientist they trusted to operate it reveals himself as Dark Beast. Before he can calibrate a journey to restore his master, X-Force tackles him through the portal, scattering them through time and space.

rules.title: Dark Beast: Scenario Rules
text: The Blue Moon, Genosha, and Savage Land sets are required for this scenario. Setting environments represent the places reached during the chase through time.

Dark Beast’s attack interrupt resolves the Special ability on the current Setting before his attack proceeds. Read the faceup Setting whenever the environment changes, because its effect changes the next attack.

setup.title: Dark Beast: Campaign Setup
bullets: After normal scenario setup, shuffle the Age of Apocalypse encounter set into the encounter deck. Select an unused mission and an available Overseer, following the mission’s campaign-log setup instructions.
Put the mission and Overseer in the mission area. The first player takes control of Mission Team on its Mission side.
Each player searches their deck for an ally to add to their opening hand. This ally counts toward the opening hand size. Expert campaign players must choose an ally sharing a trait with their hero.

victory.title: Dark Beast: Campaign Victory
bullets: Mark this mission as attempted so it cannot be selected in a later scenario. Apply its success or failure instructions in the campaign log; the selected result is shown below.
If the Overseer was defeated on its Overseer face, remove that Overseer from the campaign pool. Defeating its Prelate face does not count.

intro.title: Scenario 5: En Sabah Nur
text: After taking Dark Beast’s time machine, X-Force tries to return far enough into the past to prevent Xavier’s assassination. They arrive only in time to witness the attack.

Professor X survives long enough to reach hospital, but he is infected with the techno-organic virus. Cable knows Apocalypse has the antidote, so X-Force and the X-Men assault En Sabah Nur’s pyramid while their allies work to save the professor.

rules.title: En Sabah Nur: Scenario Rules
text: Apocalypse starts in Biomorph form and can change to Cyberpath or Giant form. A form change is not a reveal or defeat: retain his damage, hit points, attachments, and other state unless a card effect explicitly changes them.

The finale always uses Protect the Professor. Professor X cannot enter play, even through an effect that puts an ally directly into play. Defeat this mission and win the scenario to win the campaign; winning the battle with the mission unfinished loses the campaign.

setup.title: En Sabah Nur: Campaign Setup
bullets: After normal scenario setup, shuffle the Age of Apocalypse encounter set into the encounter deck and reveal Protect the Professor rather than selecting a random mission.

Select an available Overseer and set up the mission area and Mission Team normally. Each player searches for a starting ally, which counts toward their opening hand size. In expert campaign, the ally must share a trait with their hero.
Professor X cannot enter play for any reason during this game.

victory.title: En Sabah Nur: Campaign Victory
bullets: If Protect the Professor succeeded, the heroes save Professor X and win the campaign. If it did not, the campaign is lost even though this scenario was won.

rules.title: Liberate the Seattle Core: Mission Briefing
text: Set copies of Desperate Measures aside. Success gives each player a copy in hand; failure places 2 threat per player on the main scheme.

Campaign victory after mission success lets each player include one copy of Desperate Measures in future games without counting it toward minimum deck size. Mission failure removes those copies from the campaign.

success.title: Liberate the Seattle Core: Campaign Success
bullets: Each player may include one copy of Desperate Measures in future campaign games. It does not count toward minimum deck size.

failure.title: Liberate the Seattle Core: Campaign Failure
bullets: Remove Desperate Measures from the campaign.

rules.title: Evacuate Survivors: Mission Briefing
text: Each player shuffles Panicked Refugees into their deck during setup. Mission success lets each player search their deck and discard pile for a card to add to hand; mission failure deals each player an encounter card.
At campaign victory, a successful evacuation removes the Refugees and rewards an upgrade. A failed evacuation keeps Refugees in the heroes’ future decks.

success.title: Evacuate Survivors: Campaign Success
bullets: Remove Panicked Refugees from the campaign. Each player chooses an upgrade of any aspect they may include in future games, exempt from minimum deck size.

failure.title: Evacuate Survivors: Campaign Failure
bullets: Each player must shuffle Panicked Refugees into their deck during later campaign games.

rules.title: Sabotage the Sea Wall: Mission Briefing
text: Shuffle North American Sea Wall into the encounter deck during setup. Mission success removes the wall and lets each player deal 3 damage to an enemy; failure finds and reveals the wall.
At campaign victory, success permanently removes the wall and grants each player a support reward. Failure leaves the wall as a recurring campaign hazard.

success.title: Sabotage the Sea Wall: Campaign Success
bullets: Remove North American Sea Wall from the campaign. Each player chooses a support of any aspect they may include in future games, exempt from minimum deck size.

failure.title: Sabotage the Sea Wall: Campaign Failure
bullets: Shuffle North American Sea Wall into the encounter deck when setting up later campaign games.

rules.title: Find Lost Mutants: Mission Briefing
text: Set Destiny, Blink, Morph, and X-Man aside. Mission success lets each player take a different available campaign ally into hand; failure makes each player discard a card.
At campaign victory, success lets each player choose a distinct campaign ally for future games. Failure removes all four of these allies from the campaign.

success.title: Find Lost Mutants: Campaign Success
bullets: In player order, each player chooses a different available campaign ally to include in future games. The selected ally does not count toward minimum deck size.

failure.title: Find Lost Mutants: Campaign Failure
bullets: Remove Destiny, Blink, Morph, and X-Man from the campaign.

rules.title: Protect the Professor: Mission Briefing
text: This is the fixed final mission. Professor X cannot enter play while it is being fought. Mission success lets each player search deck and discard for an ally to add to hand; mission failure immediately makes the players lose.
The campaign can be won only by completing this mission and winning the En Sabah Nur scenario. A battle won while this mission remains unfinished still loses the campaign.

success.title: Protect the Professor: Campaign Success
bullets: Professor X was protected. Win the En Sabah Nur scenario as well to complete the campaign.

failure.title: Protect the Professor: Campaign Failure
bullets: Professor X was not protected. Winning the battle cannot turn this result into a campaign victory.

setup.title: Shadowland Campaign
text: Fight through Shadows in the Night, Shadow Labyrinth, and Heart of Shadow in that order. Keep the same identity throughout the campaign; aspects and legal deck contents may change between scenarios.

The campaign tracks removed Dark Protégés, whether Creeping Corruption became Overpowering, and the supports or upgrades you prepare for later scenarios. In expert campaign mode, remaining hit points also carry over. A defeat allows another attempt at the same scenario without a campaign penalty.

campaignMode.title: Shadowland: Campaign Mode
text: The Hand's fortress holds three connected adventures: Shadows in the Night, Shadow Labyrinth, and Heart of Shadow. Win all three, in order, to complete the campaign.

Use the same identity throughout. Between scenarios you may change aspects and customize your deck under the normal deck-building rules. A loss lets you reset that scenario and try again without a campaign penalty.

Normal scenario setup is followed by the campaign setup instructions. After a victory, resolve that scenario's campaign instructions before continuing. The campaign log preserves these results for the next game.
bullets: Black Flower is reserved for campaign instructions: do not select it as a scenario's optional modular encounter set during this campaign.
A Dark Protégé checked off in the campaign log is removed from the campaign and cannot appear as a villain in a later scenario.
Creeping Corruption, Overpowering results, and prepared supports or upgrades link the scenarios. Preparing a card can give you a head start, but starting with it in play adds corruption.

expertCampaign.title: Shadowland: Expert Campaign
text: Expert campaign instructions add persistent damage. After a victory, each surviving player records their remaining hit points, capped at their identity's base hit points. That recorded value determines their starting health in the next scenario.

During later scenario setup, each player may take one facedown encounter card to restore their identity to full health. A player defeated in a game their teammates win does not receive that scenario's victory benefits, but can rejoin the next game by taking this encounter card and restoring their health.
Losing a scenario allows a retry, including the final expert scenario. Expert campaign mode and the scenario's normal/expert difficulty are separate choices.

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign: Starting Health
bullets: Begin with the hit points recorded after the previous victory.
You may take one facedown encounter card to restore your identity to full health. A defeated player returning to the campaign must take this option to rejoin.

featuredRules.title: Shadowland: Featured Terms and Keywords
bullets: First Player Action: only the first player may trigger it, at a time they could take a normal action.
Creeping Corruption flips and clears its counters when it reaches five on its Setup face. Reaching five on its Overpowering face defeats its controller, so extra corruption is a lasting risk.
Assault: a character making a basic thwart against that scheme uses ATK instead of THW. An ally then takes the consequential damage printed under its ATK.

Linked: set a linked card aside when the relevant card that brings it into play is included. Linked cards cannot be included directly in a player or encounter deck and do not count toward deck-size limits.
Hinder X places X threat on a card when it enters play. Patrol prevents an engaged player from thwarting the main scheme with cards they control.
Permanent cards cannot leave play, be defeated, or have their text blanked except through abilities in their own set. Setup cards begin in play.
Piercing discards a target's tough status cards before an attack deals damage. Ranged ignores retaliate. Stalwart prevents stunned and confused status cards.
Steady characters need two stunned or confused status cards for that status to replace an activation; remove all cards of that status when it does.

Teamwork activates an entering minion against its engaged player if another minion with the named trait is in play. When a defeated Ninja brings in a replacement, discard the defeated Ninja before checking the replacement's Teamwork.
Villainous gives the activating character a boost card from the encounter deck; resolve its boost ability and icons for that activation.

intro.title: Scenario 1: Shadows in the Night
text: The Hand has raised Shadowland in the middle of Hell's Kitchen. Its ninjas enforce a cruel version of justice, terrifying the neighborhood and driving its residents into panic and street fighting.
At the fortress, a figure on the tenshu orders ninjas to form a defensive ring. Before you can break through, the mysterious commander drops into the streets to confront you.

rules.title: Shadows in the Night: Positions
text: Two environment cards track positions: one for the villain and one for the heroes. Each has The Streets Below on one face and Atop the Tenshu on the other. Changing a position flips the corresponding environment.

The positions match when both environments show the same title. They differ when the faceup titles do not match. Read position-dependent abilities using these faceup titles; the villain-position environment explains the resulting combat and thwarting effects.
bullets: The first-player movement action can change a position only once per phase.

Choosing the street effect that places 3 threat and stuns your identity is legal while already stunned, but it will not flip the environment: the complete effect must resolve before its ‘then’ instruction can happen.

setup.title: Shadows in the Night: Campaign Setup
bullets: Record the heroes chosen for the campaign. If Daredevil or Elektra is a player identity, remove the villain with that name from this campaign.
Each player starts with the Setup face of Creeping Corruption in play. Set aside any unused copies and shuffle the remaining Black Flower cards into the encounter deck.
Place 1 additional threat per player on the main scheme.

victory.title: Shadows in the Night: Victory
bullets: Remove this scenario's Dark Protégé villain from the campaign; that villain cannot be selected in later scenarios.
Each surviving player records whether their Creeping Corruption has the Overpowering trait.

Each surviving player may record one support or upgrade they control with a printed cost of 2 or less. A card with no cost, shown as a dash, is ineligible. A later scenario lets you start with a recorded card in play in exchange for corruption.
In expert campaign mode, record each surviving identity's remaining hit points, up to its base hit points.

intro.title: Scenario 2: Shadow Labyrinth
text: Inside Shadowland, the fortress itself becomes your opponent. Corridors rearrange, paths turn into dead ends, and hidden mechanisms threaten intruders with darts, tripwires, and other traps.
A shadowy attacker appears to strike, then disappears when you begin to prevail. With the walls moving around you, you must keep pressing toward the fortress's heart.

rules.title: Shadow Labyrinth: Traps and Passages
bullets: The separate trap deck begins with the seven Trap! treacheries from Deadly Contraptions and Whisper in the Dark from Shadow Labyrinth. Trap! cards from any additional modular sets also belong in this deck.

A trap-deck reveal resolves its top card normally. Discard cards with the Trap! trait to the trap discard pile; cards without that trait go to the encounter discard pile, even when revealed from the trap deck.
When the trap deck runs out, reshuffle its discard pile. This does not reset the encounter deck and does not add an acceleration token.
Surge on a card revealed from the trap deck still deals its additional card from the ordinary encounter deck.
Shifting Corridors has infinite hit points. It can take damage but cannot be defeated by damage; use the scenario's card abilities to progress through the labyrinth.
Passage counters are your remaining time. If Shifting Corridors runs out of passage counters, the players lose.

setup.title: Shadow Labyrinth: Campaign Setup
bullets: Each player starts with a fresh Setup-side Creeping Corruption. Set aside unused copies and shuffle the remaining Black Flower cards into the encounter deck.
If your corruption was Overpowering in the previous scenario, place 1 corruption counter on your Creeping Corruption.
You may take one copy of the support or upgrade recorded after the previous victory from your deck and start with it in play. If you do, add 1 corruption counter.
Place 3 additional threat per player on the main scheme.

victory.title: Shadow Labyrinth: Victory
bullets: Each surviving player records whether their Creeping Corruption is Overpowering.

Each surviving player may record one support or upgrade they control with a printed cost of 2 or less. Cards with a dash instead of a cost are ineligible. In the final scenario, starting with a recorded card in play costs additional corruption.
In expert campaign mode, record each surviving identity's remaining hit points, up to its base hit points.

intro.title: Scenario 3: Heart of Shadow
text: You reach Krahllak, the Hand's leader, in the final chamber. His ritual threatens to extend its corruption across New York, ensnaring the people in its reach.
When you attack, Krahllak turns that power against you. He tempts you to give in to the corruption and join his Dark Protégés. Stop the ritual and bring down Shadowland before your own resolve fails.

rules.title: Heart of Shadow: Creeping Corruption
text: The finale includes Creeping Corruption as part of its normal scenario setup. Keep track of its current face as well as its counters: the Overpowering face represents a dangerous loss of control.
bullets: Reaching five corruption counters on the Setup face flips the upgrade and clears its counters. Reaching five on its Overpowering face defeats its controller.

Krahllak's attack interrupt asks the attacked player whether to resolve it before another player decides whether to defend that attack. A teammate defending later does not change who makes that earlier choice.

setup.title: Heart of Shadow: Campaign Setup
bullets: For each previous scenario in which your corruption was recorded as Overpowering, place 1 corruption counter on your Creeping Corruption.
You may take one copy of each recorded support or upgrade from your deck and start with those cards in play. Add 1 corruption counter for each card you put into play this way.

Randomly deal Archpriestess, Gorgon, Lady Bullseye, and White Tiger from the Dark Protégé set: each player receives one as a facedown encounter card. Shuffle any remaining minions into the encounter deck.

victory.title: Shadowland: Campaign Complete
text: With Heart of Shadow defeated, you have won all three scenarios and completed the Shadowland campaign.

campaignMode.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.: Campaign Mode
text: Investigate an A.I.M. kidnapping operation and expose a mole within the S.H.I.E.L.D. Executive Board. Play Black Widow, Batroc, M.O.D.O.K., Thunderbolts, and Baron Zemo in that order. Results from each mission change later missions.

Keep the same identity throughout the campaign. Between scenarios, you may change aspects and customize your deck using the normal deck-building rules. Complete ordinary scenario setup, then the campaign setup instructions before drawing opening hands; evidence instructions resolve after mulligans.

After a victory, resolve the mission’s victory instructions and keep the resulting campaign records. A defeat normally allows another attempt without a penalty. The final mission has additional replay rules, and losing it in an expert campaign ends the campaign.

evidence.title: The Investigation: Means, Motive, and Opportunity
text: One board member is secretly collaborating with A.I.M. Their identity is determined by three hidden evidence cards: one means, one motive, and one opportunity. The game selects these without revealing them and keeps the other six evidence cards available to discover.

Earned evidence rules out every combination containing that evidence. Use the remaining combinations in the campaign log to deduce the mole. The hidden evidence and undiscovered evidence remain secret between scenarios.

Evidence is kept in the campaign log rather than added to a deck. Its Setup ability helps the players in later missions. Learning a card during a scenario does not immediately resolve its Setup ability.

board.title: The S.H.I.E.L.D. Executive Board
text: The three board members begin as environments with secret counters representing A.I.M.’s leverage over them. Their abilities let you uncover those secrets and receive assistance. If a mission is won with at least one Board Member environment having no secrets, the campaign gains one evidence card.

A.I.M. Interference adds secrets. A board member with four secrets, or three in expert scenario mode, betrays the heroes and flips to its attachment side. That side strengthens the villain and punishes additional secrets.
Secret counters and betrayals persist between missions. A board member who has betrayed the heroes remains on its attachment side for the rest of the campaign.

expertCampaign.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.: Expert Campaign
text: After winning a mission, surviving players record their remaining hit points, capped at their identity’s base hit points. These become their starting hit points in the next mission.

During later setup, each player may add one secret to a Board Member environment to heal damage equal to their identity’s REC. A defeated player can rejoin the campaign using this recovery opportunity.
A defeated player does not take part in the victory instructions for the mission their teammates won. Losing the final Baron Zemo mission loses the entire expert campaign.

laterSetup.title: Campaign Setup: Board and Evidence
bullets: Restore each board member’s recorded secrets and betrayed side. For the first four missions, include all three A.I.M. Interference treacheries in the encounter deck.

After mulligans, resolve the Setup ability of each earned evidence card. Each player may pay its stated secret-counter cost to add an eligible card from their collection, then may pay its stated threat cost to search their deck for an eligible card.

When the same evidence card offers collection additions to multiple players, those players must select different card titles. The card added by evidence may exceed the ordinary deck-building copy limit.

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Setup: Persistent Damage
bullets: Set each identity to its remaining hit points recorded after the previous mission.
Each player may place one secret on a Board Member environment to heal damage equal to their identity’s REC. A player recorded at zero hit points must recover in order to rejoin.

recordBoard.title: Campaign Victory: Board and Evidence
bullets: Record each board member’s remaining secrets and any betrayal.
If at least one Board Member environment has no secret counters, gain one evidence card and eliminate the combinations containing its evidence icon from the investigation.

expertVictory.title: Expert Campaign Victory
bullets: Record each surviving identity’s remaining hit points, never more than its base hit points. Record defeated identities at zero for the next mission’s recovery instructions.

intro.title: Black Widow: A Missing Specialist
text: S.H.I.E.L.D. computer specialist Sarah Garza has disappeared. An Inhuman cocoon found in her Brooklyn apartment suggests that her dormant genes have activated, but the extent of her new powers is unknown.

While investigating Garza’s disappearance and rumors of a mole on the Executive Board, you trace her phone to a disused subway tunnel. An A.I.M. base awaits there, protected by Yelena Belova: the Black Widow.

rules.title: Black Widow: Preparation Abilities
bullets: Preparation abilities replace Boost abilities on cards in Black Widow’s encounter set. Turning such a card faceup as a boost does not resolve its Preparation ability.

Before a hero or ally’s attack against Black Widow resolves, her Forced Interrupt removes threat from the main scheme. If it removes threat, discard the encounter deck’s top card and resolve any Preparation ability on that card before continuing the attack. If it removes no threat, the rest of that interrupt does not resolve.
Damage from an effect that is not an attack does not trigger this interrupt.

setup.title: Black Widow: Campaign Setup
bullets: Record the campaign’s chosen identities, prepare the hidden evidence, and put the three Board Member environments into play with two secrets each.
Shuffle all three A.I.M. Interference treacheries into the encounter deck.

victory.title: Black Widow: Campaign Victory
bullets: Record the combined number of minions and side schemes still in play. This determines the starting Alert Level during the embassy mission.
Then record the Executive Board’s secrets and check whether the heroes earn evidence.

intro.title: Batroc: The Embassy Rescue
text: Black Widow remains silent, but captured A.I.M. operatives reveal a kidnapping network supplying A.I.M. Island. The victims appear to be passing through that country’s embassy in Washington, D.C.
You enter the embassy without Executive Board approval to find and extract the missing people. If caught, you will face the consequences without official S.H.I.E.L.D. support.

rules.title: Batroc: Infiltrating the Embassy
bullets: Win by clearing threat from the three main-scheme stages rather than by defeating Batroc. The first stage represents entering the embassy.
Each time stage two reaches zero threat, rescue a captive. You may reset its threat to three per player to rescue another captive, or advance to the escape stage.
Clear the final stage before all Rescued Captive allies are defeated to win the mission.

Batroc has a fixed hit point value rather than a per-player value. His zero-hit-point interrupt grants its printed benefit and resets his hit points; it replaces defeating him and does not count as a villain defeat.

setup.title: Batroc: Campaign Setup
bullets: Add threat to Alert Level equal to the combined minions and side schemes recorded after Black Widow. Restore the Executive Board, then resolve earned evidence after mulligans.

victory.title: Batroc: Campaign Victory
bullets: Record the number of Rescued Captive allies still in play. This reduces the extra lock counters in the M.O.D.O.K. mission.
Then record the Executive Board’s secrets and check whether the heroes earn evidence.

intro.title: M.O.D.O.K.: A.I.M. Island
text: The embassy captives are free, but Sarah Garza is still missing. Evidence points to A.I.M. Island, where M.O.D.O.K. is using kidnapped Inhumans as genetic templates for super-powered Adaptoids.
The investigation also implicates an unidentified Executive Board member. With the Board compromised, you undertake another unauthorized rescue mission.

rules.title: M.O.D.O.K.: The Holding Cells
bullets: The Holding Cell deck contains four double-sided cards with Inhuman allies on their reverse sides. Only its top card is in play. Each cell receives its printed lock counters as it enters play.

Free all four Inhuman allies by removing the cells’ locks, then reduce M.O.D.O.K. to zero hit points to win. Use the cells’ Hero Actions, M.O.D.O.K.’s zero-hit-point interrupt, and encounter-card effects to remove locks.
Before the final rescue, M.O.D.O.K.’s zero-hit-point interrupt replaces his defeat, provides its printed benefit, and resets his fixed hit point value.

setup.title: M.O.D.O.K.: Campaign Setup
bullets: Add three lock counters per player to the top Holding Cell, then remove one lock counter per player for each Rescued Captive recorded after Batroc.
Restore the Executive Board and resolve earned evidence after mulligans.

victory.title: M.O.D.O.K.: Campaign Victory
bullets: Record which Adaptoid environments remain in play. These return during the final Baron Zemo mission.
Then record the Executive Board’s secrets and check whether the heroes earn evidence.

intro.title: Thunderbolts: Under Arrest
text: After rescuing the Inhumans and returning them home, you arrive in Washington to find the Thunderbolts waiting for you. Their leader, Citizen V, says the Executive Board has authorized your arrest for the operation on A.I.M. Island.

rules.title: Thunderbolts: Backup and Engagement
bullets: Thunderbolt Backup hosts a Thunderbolt minion that remains in play and keeps its tokens, status cards, and attachments. You may attack it and target it with player-card abilities, but it does not activate while it is not engaged with a player.
Attacking a Thunderbolt triggers the main scheme’s response that makes that minion engage the attacker’s player, including a minion attached to Thunderbolt Backup.

Thunderbolt Backup moves the most-damaged Thunderbolt in play onto itself and heals it. If another minion was attached, that minion engages the player who had been engaged with the incoming minion. If the already-attached minion is most damaged, it stays there and heals.

If an effect attacks an ally directly, players may defend normally. An undefended attack damages that ally; boost references to “you” refer to its controller, and abilities requiring the enemy to attack your identity do not trigger. Overkill excess goes to the defeated ally’s controller’s identity.

setup.title: Thunderbolts: Campaign Setup
bullets: Restore the Executive Board’s recorded secrets and betrayed sides, include A.I.M. Interference, and resolve earned evidence after mulligans.

This scenario uses one Thunderbolt modular encounter set per player, plus one additional set. Each must contain an Elite Thunderbolt minion; the included qualifying sets are Gravitational Pull, Hard Sound, Pale Little Spider, Power of the Atom, Supersonic, and The Leaper.

victory.title: Thunderbolts: Campaign Victory
bullets: Record the names of Thunderbolt minions still in play. They and their encounter sets can return in the final mission, except Jolt’s set.
Then record the Executive Board’s secrets and check whether the heroes earn evidence.

intro.title: Baron Zemo: Expose the Mole
text: Citizen V is revealed to be Baron Helmut Zemo, and the Thunderbolts are his Masters of Evil in disguise. S.H.I.E.L.D. arrives, but its agents take you into custody rather than arresting Zemo. The Executive Board already knew who he was.

With Agent Coulson’s help, you escape confinement and search for proof linking Zemo to A.I.M. Find the mole before Zemo turns the entire Board against you, while avoiding unnecessary harm to fellow S.H.I.E.L.D. agents.

rules.title: Baron Zemo: Evidence and the Accusation
bullets: During stage one, remove secrets from Board Member environments to gather the evidence needed to identify the mole. At the end of the player phase, the main scheme can place two secrets on a board environment with no secrets to gain evidence. Evidence learned now provides information; ignore its Setup text during play.
Reducing Zemo to zero hit points before his final form removes secrets through his printed interrupt and resets his fixed hit point value; it does not defeat him.

You may advance to the accusation even with incomplete evidence. Choose a means, motive, and opportunity combination that the earned evidence has not ruled out. That combination also names the accused board member.

The game reveals the actual hidden combination. Each incorrect means, motive, opportunity, or board-member guess adds one secret to every board member. Accusing the wrong board member also adds three secrets to that member.

Advance to the final stage, reveal Zemo’s Unmasked side, and attach the exposed mole to him. The scheme receives threat for secrets on Board Member attachments. Defeat this version of Zemo to win. If all three board members join him, the heroes lose.
A premature accusation can make the battle harder, but being wrong does not itself lose the scenario. Waiting for certainty may be riskier if the main scheme is close to completion.

setup.title: Baron Zemo: Campaign Setup
bullets: Restore each Adaptoid environment recorded after M.O.D.O.K. and add all copies of the Adaptoid minion to the encounter deck.
Add the recorded surviving Thunderbolt minions and their encounter sets, except Jolt’s set.
Keep the campaign’s hidden and earned evidence, restore recorded board-member secrets and betrayals, and resolve earned evidence after mulligans.

standardDefeat.title: Baron Zemo: If the Heroes Lose
text: In a standard campaign, you may retry the final mission. Prepare a new hidden means, motive, and opportunity combination and a new supply of discoverable evidence.

Before repeating the mission’s campaign setup, gain one evidence card for each earlier scenario in which a Board Member environment finished with no secrets. The investigation therefore starts again with the evidence rewards you previously earned.

expertDefeat.title: Baron Zemo: Expert Campaign Defeat
text: Losing this mission in an expert campaign ends the campaign: S.H.I.E.L.D. arrests the heroes and convicts them of the accusations made against them.

victory.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.: Campaign Victory
text: Zemo is defeated and the mole is exposed. The heroes are cleared of the charges against them and win the campaign.

intro.title: Fear No Evil
text: A coordinated crime wave is sweeping New York City. Protect its neighborhoods, stop the underlings behind each crisis, and uncover the mastermind directing the chaos.

campaignMode.title: Campaign Mode
text: Keep the same identity throughout the campaign; aspects and deck contents can change between games under the usual deck-building rules.

Five interchangeable scenarios can be tackled in the order your group chooses. Each pairs its main scheme with an underling villain. Once all five scenarios are Completed or Failed, confront Kingpin in the finale.
bullets: An underling already recorded beside a scenario remains assigned to it on a retry. Otherwise, use an unassigned underling.
For a first campaign, the recommended order is Hammerhead, Bullseye, Electro, then Purple Man and Typhoid Mary in either order. Later campaigns use random assignments.

A scenario victory provides its Completed campaign environment for later games. A Failed scenario provides the penalty on its Failed side instead. You may inspect both sides before choosing a scenario.
A loss does not immediately mark the scenario Failed. The campaign continues through its planning and progression steps.

planning.title: Choose Which Crisis to Face
text: Before choosing the next scenario, the app randomly selects two unresolved scenarios and adds one progress mark to each. If only one remains, it receives two marks. A scenario fails as soon as it reaches three marks.

After progression, choose any scenario that is neither Completed nor Failed. If none remain, the next battle is Kingpin. The app records progression and the chosen underling; continuing this briefing does not choose your scenario.

expertCampaign.title: Expert Campaign
text: After every game, record each hero's remaining hit points, capped at that identity's base hit points. Those become the hero's starting hit points in the next game.

During player setup, each player may take one facedown encounter card to heal damage equal to their REC. A defeated hero can rejoin the next scenario by using this healing step. A defeated player does not take part in victory instructions if teammates win.
bullets: Follow the instructions marked Expert Campaign Only as well as the ordinary campaign instructions.
Losing an interchangeable scenario adds one progress mark to that scenario before the next planning step.
If you lose the Kingpin finale, flip one Completed campaign environment to its Failed side and retry. If no Completed environment remains, the campaign is lost.

campaignSetup.title: Campaign Setup
text: The app applies the campaign log after the scenario and player setup steps. Each Completed or Failed environment returns on its recorded side and resolves its Setup ability.
Remove from your deck every ally or support whose title is recorded as removed from the campaign. Before starting a new game, replace cards as necessary to meet the normal minimum deck size.

If trust with Mary was established and the Mary ally has not been defeated, the group chooses a player to begin with the Typhoid Mary campaign ally. Scenario-specific campaign penalties are applied after these shared steps.

expertVictory.title: Expert Campaign: Remaining Hit Points
text: The app records surviving heroes' remaining hit points, capped at their base hit points, for the next scenario. Heroes defeated during the game are recorded with zero hit points and can rejoin through the next game's healing step.

expertDefeat.title: Expert Campaign: After a Defeat
text: The app records remaining hit points after a loss as well as after a win. Losing an interchangeable scenario adds one progress mark to it; it only becomes Failed if this brings it to three marks.
After a Kingpin defeat, choose a Completed campaign environment to turn to its Failed side before retrying. If there are none, the campaign ends in defeat.

bullseye.title: Your Underling: Bullseye
text: Bullseye adds a boost icon to each of his boost cards. Extra boost cards can make his attacks especially dangerous.

His encounter cards can remove allies and Persona supports from the game; a campaign victory can permanently bar those titles from your decks. Bullseye II has Adamantium-Laced Spine, which limits damage from an attack to 3 until you flip it. Favor several small attacks while its protection is active.

electro.title: Your Underling: Electro
text: Electro stores charge counters on Electric Charge and spends them to gain additional boost cards. Scheming and encounter effects replenish the charges.
Players can spend resources to remove charge counters. Energy resources remove charges efficiently, but some of her encounter effects punish heroes with energy resources.

hammerhead.title: Your Underling: Hammerhead
text: Hammerhead stuns characters he damages. His Head First! treachery and Maggia Underboss minions become more dangerous while your hero is stunned.
Preventing all damage, defending effectively, or using an ally to absorb an attack can protect your hero from the stun.

purpleMan.title: Your Underling: Purple Man
text: Purple Man uses his low printed stats to disguise a dangerous encounter-card engine: his cards gain a boost ability that deals the card as a facedown encounter card after the activation.

His Influenced minions punish you for defeating them. They have vulnerable, so stunning or confusing them discards them safely instead. Purple Man grants them guard, with additional villainous and patrol at higher stages.

typhoidMary.title: Your Underling: Typhoid Mary
text: Mary begins on a random face and flips after each villain phase. Her attack and scheme strengths change with her face, so plan around the coming activation.

Win by placing three tokens on Disturbed Psyche rather than by defeating successive villain stages. Clearing Establish Trust adds a threat token; reducing the villain to zero hit points adds a damage token.
A victory with at least two threat tokens on Disturbed Psyche establishes trust in the campaign and can make Mary available as an ally in later games.

intro.title: Protection Racket
text: A shopkeeper is being threatened for protection money. You arrive as armed thugs smash the business, only to discover their boss is joining the attack.

rules.title: Protection Racket: Scenario Rules
text: Each player has a separate business main scheme in their play area. In standard mode, inspect the business reverse faces before choosing one.

An event, treachery, or card in a player’s play area that refers to “the main scheme” affects that player’s business. Cards outside player play areas, including the villain, side schemes, and environments, apply such references to every business.
An effect referring to “a scheme”, including a basic thwart, can choose any eligible main scheme. Acceleration icons and acceleration tokens add threat to every business during the villain phase.

setup.title: Protection Racket: Campaign Setup
bullets: For each progress mark beside Protection Racket, add 1 threat to every business main scheme, or 2 threat in expert scenario mode.

victory.title: Protection Racket: Victory

intro.title: Art Museum Heist

rules.title: Art Museum Heist: Scenario Rules
text: Four Art attachments can change hands during this scenario. One randomly chosen piece starts attached to the villain. Art increases its host’s SCH or THW, and each piece on the villain adds another 1 threat per player to the villain-phase main-scheme placement.
Use an Art attachment’s Hero Action to take it for your hero. Three pieces give their new host a status card; Inspiring Pottery grants stalwart, which removes stunned and confused statuses.

After an enemy makes an undefended attack against an identity with Art, move one Art attachment from that identity to the villain. Both villain and minion attacks can trigger this, but only one piece moves per attack.

intro.title: The Getaway
text: Police are pursuing a bank robber through Hell’s Kitchen. You move to cut off the getaway car before it reaches the tunnel, but a near collision forces you into a running chase.

rules.title: The Getaway: Scenario Rules
text: Speed counters represent an increasingly dangerous chase. The main scheme gains a speed counter at the end of a round unless it is clear of threat. There is no limit, and encounter effects become harsher as speed rises.

While the villain is Out Front, damage that would be dealt to the villain removes that much main-scheme threat instead. Because damage is not dealt, tough remains on the villain and no damage is placed on a Vehicle attachment.

When the main scheme has no threat, Out Front flips to Alongside and resolves its When Revealed collision damage. Alongside flips back to Out Front at the end of a round with threat on the main scheme.

rules.title: Stop the Presses!: Scenario Rules
text: Each player starts with a random Daily Bugle support with 3 stamina counters. These supports are discarded when their last stamina counter is removed; if a Daily Bugle support leaves play, the players lose.

Use the Daily Bugle environment’s ability to replenish a support before its stamina runs out.

intro.title: Kingpin
text: After fighting crises across the city, you realize the crime wave has been orchestrated. Public anger has been directed at the heroes, and Kingpin is the obvious beneficiary. Then an explosion below draws you back into danger: your nemesis is calling you out.

rules.title: Kingpin: Nemeses and Public Support
text: This scenario does not use the Standard encounter set. Expert scenario mode still uses the Expert set.

Each player reveals their set-aside nemesis minion during setup. If that minion shares a title with a character already in play, remove it from the game and reveal an Underling minion from the encounter deck instead. Nemesis cards introduced this way become part of the encounter deck.
Kingpin starts on side 1, manipulating events from behind the scenes. He cannot take damage, be stunned or confused, or have upgrades attached. When he would attack, he schemes instead.

Defeat minions to build Public Support. At the start of a villain phase, enough support flips Kingpin to side 2, advances the main scheme, and turns Public Support to its High side. You can then attack Kingpin, but Endgame gives every minion guard.

setup.title: Kingpin: Campaign Setup
bullets: With at least three Completed campaign environments in play, give every minion currently in play tough.
With at least four Completed environments, also find and reveal James Wesley.

victory.title: Kingpin Defeated
text: You have brought down Kingpin and won the Fear No Evil campaign.

defeat.title: Kingpin: Defeat
text: In a standard campaign, retry Kingpin.
In an expert campaign, choose one Completed campaign environment and flip it to its Failed side, then retry. If no Completed environment is available, the players lose the campaign.
